justification: Inspected src/main/java/org/apache/commons/io/input/CountingInputStream.java and src/test/java/org/apache/commons/io/input/CountingInputStreamTest.java. The class is small (about 128 source lines), has one field (`count`), and only one responsibility: incrementing a byte counter on reads/skips and exposing/resetting that counter. Its API is narrow (constructors plus `afterRead`, `getByteCount`, `getCount`, `resetByteCount`, `resetCount`, and `skip`), and the tests exercise only counting behavior, EOF, reset, and skip. This does not show the multiple responsibilities, large method set, or low cohesion typical of insufficient modularization.
